What Are Medical Billing & Coding Audits?

A Routine Check-Up for Your Billing, Before a Payer Runs One For You

A medical billing and coding audit is a structured review of a practice's claims, coding choices and supporting documentation, checked against payer rules and current compliance standards. Auditors inspect patient charts and billing records the same way a payer eventually will, but with time to fix what's wrong before it becomes a denial, an overpayment demand, or a compliance investigation.

Skipping audits doesn't make billing errors disappear, it just delays who finds them. Improper coding, incomplete documentation, missed charges and noncompliance with reimbursement guidelines all sit quietly in a billing system until a payer or regulator surfaces them, usually with a penalty attached.

PMEX audits are designed to catch those issues first, correct them proactively, and strengthen the revenue cycle before a payer ever has a reason to look twice.

Audit Methodology

Five Lenses, Applied to Every Engagement

Audits can be scoped by timing (before or after submission) and by scope (internal team or independent review). PMEX applies whichever combination fits the problem you're trying to solve.

Internal Audit

In-depth review of your own processes and documentation against industry standards.

External Audit

Independent review of claims and payments from third-party payers like Medicare and Medicaid.

Prospective Audit

Claims checked for accuracy and completeness before they are ever submitted.

Retrospective Audit

Claims reviewed after payer processing to correct errors and appeal denials.

Comprehensive Audit

A holistic pass across coding, billing, documentation and compliance together.

What We Examine

Four Areas Where Revenue Usually Hides or Leaks

Coding Accuracy

Charts reviewed to confirm codes match the diagnosis, procedures performed and complexity level, catching both upcoding and undercoding before they become a compliance or revenue problem.

Charge Capture Accuracy

Documentation is compared line by line against the itemized billing statement to find services and supplies that were delivered but never billed.

Documentation Compliance

The record is checked for the clarity, consistency and completeness a payer requires to accept a claim, flagging vague notes, missing signatures and gaps in medical necessity.

Payer Contract Accuracy

Fee schedules and payer contract terms are checked against what was actually billed and paid, and billing system data entry is verified for accuracy.

Medical Chart Reviews & Validations

Deeper Reviews for Specific Data Questions

Medical Chart Reviews Risk Adjustment Data Validation Data Abstraction Review Charge Validation

Chart reviews span inpatient, outpatient, radiology and other specialty records, assessing care quality, coding and documentation standards, and clinical guideline adherence. Risk adjustment validation checks diagnosis codes, HCCs and risk scores for accuracy. Data abstraction pulls and verifies diagnoses, procedures, medications and lab results against what's entered in the EHR. Charge validation confirms that what was billed is actually supported by the chart, catching both undercharges and overcharges.
